text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- SIGNS OF IMPROVED PUBLIC SECTOR ACCOUNTS

Public sector accounts are showing the first signs of improvement, with the consolidated operational public sector deficit falling to 2.3 percent of gross domestic product in the first two months of this year from 3.85 percent in December 1996.
Finance Minister Pedro Malan said the election calendar would not set the course for the government's economic policy, which would continue to implement the measures which were necessary.
A national poll shows 31 percent of Brazilians think members of Congress are doing a bad job, the worst approval rating since the current legislature took office.
-- ONLY FOUR PCT OF LAND REFORM FUNDS USED
Until March, the government spent only four percent of the funds earmarked for land reform in 1997.
-- RIO POLICE BLAMES DRUG TRAFFICKING FOR 50 PCT OF MURDERS
Police say drug wars between traffickers are responsible for half of the murders in Rio de Janeiro.
-- HOMELESS COPY LANDLESS' STRATEGY OF INVASIONS
Homeless people in Sao Paulo have formed a movement to secure housing inspired by the success of the Landless Movement's strategy of invading large farm properties.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
